subject: Post-demo: real-time QA engine recommendations & risk summary
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: real-time QA engine recommendations & risk summary

Hi Samira / Jamal —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Below is a concise post-demo recap with a recommended shortlist, why each engine made the list, and the operational / quality risks we want to guard against if you pick an engine for the real-time QA use case.

Quick context: Helix wants sub-250ms median inference for short questions (<= 64 tokens), P95 ideally under 450ms, and cost sensitivity at 1M queries / month. You also flagged a hard requirement for stable answer accuracy on your domain-specific KB (financial summaries).

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs summary):

1) Velox-3B-int8
   - Why: Excellent median latency (p50 ~ 90ms on a single A10x4 serving config with batching tuned for 10 concurrent requests), lowest cost per 1M tokens in our bench (~$220) because of int8 execution and dense KV cache hit improvements.
   - Quality: Strong on short-answer precision after a small domain-tuning prompt set; occasional hallucination on multi-hop questions.
   - Risk / guardrails: Add targeted regression checks on your 200-domain QA prompts; enable prefix KV caching for repeat queries.

2) Citrine-7B-qat
   - Why: Better open-domain accuracy for multi-hop QA and better factual grounding on our finetuned prompts (0.5–1.2% higher exact-match on your sample eval). p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 420ms in our snapshot tests.
   - Cost: Mid-range (~$420 / 1M tokens).
   - Risk / guardrails: Slightly higher variance in latency under burst. Recommend autoscaling policy + per-route fallback to Velox-3B-int8 for latency-critical endpoints.

3) Atlas-13B-fp16 (compat mode)
   - Why: Best overall quality for complex reasoning / summarization tasks; larger context support if you expand past 512 tokens.
   - Latency: p50 ~ 260ms, p95 ~ 620ms (higher).
   - Cost: Highest (~$1,100 / 1M tokens).
   - Risk / guardrails: Not ideal for tight latency SLAs; use for non-real-time batch summarization or as a fallback for ambiguous cases to improve precision.

Immediate operational asks / proposed next steps:
- Please confirm the three models above are worth an evaluation sprint (we can run 72-hour side-by-side tests).
- Share a 1k-sample of production-like queries (we provided a safe sample outline in the attached prompt pack).
- We will provide an eval dashboard (link below) and a short prompt set for targeted regression checks.
- Ops: please confirm IP whitelist for our eval pool (we'll need 3 IPs) and whether you prefer dedicated capacity or hosted with reserved compute for the sprint.

Attachments / links I included:
- realtime_prompt_pack_v1.zip (sample prompts, negative examples, metadata mapping)
- latency_cost_estimates_helix.xlsx (config options, cost sensitivity curves)
- Eval dashboard: https://app.redwood.io/evals/helix-realtime-2028

Concise next milestone proposal:
1) You confirm shortlist and send sample queries by Friday (6/9).
2) We spin up a 72-hour eval (with metrics dashboard) and a small canary route for production-like traffic.
3) End of sprint: decision on engine + rollout plan (canary thresholds + regression guardrails).

If it helps, I can hop on a 30-min ops call with Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (model ops) to lock the config.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0198

Diego —

Thanks for the crisp recap and the shortlist. A few quick clarifying Qs before we confirm: 
- For Velox-3B-int8, can you confirm P95 under 250ms on infra comparable to our us-west-2 region (we're sensitive to cross-region noise)?
- For Citrine-7B-qat, what's the estimated cost for 1M *queries* (not tokens) assuming our median query is ~40 tokens outbound + 30 tokens in generation?
- For Atlas-13B-fp16, any way to get P95 under 500ms if we accept higher instances (we're exploring a hybrid approach for tricky prompts)?

Also, we'd like a short canary plan template from you — what thresholds would Redwood recommend for rollback (latency/error/answer-drift)?

We're inclined to run the eval sprint but want to confirm those items first. I'll loop Jamal from infra once we have the IPs to whitelist.

— Samira
Samira Khan
Product Lead, Search & QA | Helix AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@helix.ai>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@helix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: real-time QA engine recommendations & risk summary

Samira —

Answers inline + a proposed canary template below.

> Velox-3B-int8 P95 under 250ms in us-west-2?
Short answer: Yes, for short queries (~<=64 tokens) when run on our optimized pool (A10x4 equivalent) with batching tuned to 8–12 and prefix KV caching enabled. Our bench: p50 92ms, p95 230–260ms (variance depends on cross-tenant burst). We'll include per-route telemetry during the sprint.

> Citrine 7B cost for 1M queries (median size: 70 tokens total)
Estimate: ~70 tokens * 1M = 70M tokens. At our mid-range estimate (~$0.006 / 1k tokens effective for Citrine on reserved capacity), that's roughly $420. Exact number depends on prompt length variability and cache hit rate — see attached latency_cost_estimates_helix.xlsx for a sensitivity table.

> Atlas 13B P95 under 500ms with heavier instances?
Possible with larger multi-GPU pinned instances and aggressive batching, but that increases cost and may impact concurrency. For the sprint we recommend using Atlas as an asynchronous/fallback path (send ambiguous prompts to Atlas for higher-quality answers) rather than the primary route. If you want a hard SLA for Atlas-backed route, we can produce a dedicated capacity quote (I asked Marissa to prepare a rough estimate).

Proposed Canary template (suggested thresholds):
- Canary window: 1 hour at 1% of production traffic (min 200 requests)
- Latency: rollback if P95 exceeds baseline + 25% or absolute P95 > 500ms for primary route
- Error rate: rollback if 5xx or model errors > 0.5% vs baseline
- Answer drift / quality: automated regression checks fail on a sampled prompt set (more than 3/50 critical prompts degrade by >1.5% exact-match)
- Manual review: all failing canaries trigger an ops channel notification and a 30-min incident triage call

Operational notes for the sprint:
- We'll need the whitelist for these eval IPs: 52.26.17.11, 52.26.17.12, 52.26.17.13
- We'll provision a hosted reserved pool unless you request Dedicated for stricter isolation.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm rough cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted reserved for Citrine and Atlas? Marissa, can you also surface a 72-hour runbook template to attach to Samira after we get confirmation?

Attaching: realtime_prompt_pack_v1.zip, latency_cost_estimates_helix.xlsx. Eval dashboard link also included in the first message.

Thanks —
Diego
